mainTopic: חמץ that seems to have moved, רבא's questions on crumbs, animals and the effort required in בדיקה, and the משנה on when one searches
overview: The גמרא first looks at חמץ that was put in one corner and later found in another. It ties this case to a מחלוקת in a ברייתא about a lost axe, and uses חסורי מחסרא to show that the ברייתא really includes a corner case. Next, רבא rules on crumbs found after a mouse or a child carried bread in. After a mouse you must search again, but after a child you do not need to. רבא then asks a ladder of questions about mice and a חולדה carrying bread in and out of the house, and these end in תיקו. He asks a second ladder about how much effort is required to remove חמץ: a ladder for a high beam, a ladder for a pit, and paying a snake charmer. These also end in תיקו. A new משנה brings רבי יהודה's three search times and the חכמים's make-up searches, even after פסח. The גמרא first explains רבי יהודה's view with three פסוקים, then drops that explanation after רב יוסף's objection. It concludes that the real argument is whether we make a גזירה against searching once eating חמץ is forbidden. It then begins to challenge that גזירה using the עומר markets, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: חמץ placed in one corner and found in another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new case. חמץ was put in one corner and later found in a different corner. It says the case depends on a מחלוקת between רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he put [the חמץ] in this corner and found it in another corner, this is the מחלוקת between רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new בדיקת חמץ case and says the answer depends on a known מחלוקת. This line sets up the next step, where the source for that מחלוקת is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the חמץ he found is the same piece he put down, which only moved. The other option is that the original piece was taken away, and this is a different piece. If it is the same piece, the house is fine. If not, the original חמץ is still missing and he must search again.

phrases.english: If he placed [chametz] in this corner
and found [it] in another corner

phrases.aramaic: פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: it is the dispute of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and the Rabbis

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier list of doubtful בדיקה cases with a new one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether חמץ found in another corner needs a new search depends on the מחלוקת between רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the רבנן.

steps.title: The ברייתא of the lost axe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא. An axe is lost in a house. The רבנן say the house is טמא, because an impure person may have come in and taken it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the house is טהור, because the owner probably lent it out or moved it and forgot.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: An axe that was lost in a house, the house is impure, for I say an impure person entered there and took it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: the house is pure, for I say he lent it to someone else and forgot, or he took it from this corner and put it in the other corner and forgot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source of the מחלוקת it just mentioned. This is a ברייתא about טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן explain the missing axe by saying an outsider came in. That outsider could have been טמא and made the house impure. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל explains it by the owner's own forgetfulness, so nothing impure entered. Applied to חמץ, the רבנן's view points to 'someone else moved things,' while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view points to 'the owner moved it himself.'

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
For I say (a reasoning based on what most likely happened)

steps.confusionAlert: Read as written, this ברייתא only talks about a lost axe. The words about corners appear only in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's explanation. That gap is exactly what the next step asks about.

phrases.english: As it was taught: an axe that was lost in a house
the house is impure

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: אָדָם טָמֵא נִכְנַס לְשָׁם וּנְטָלוֹ.
phrases.english: for I say: an impure person entered there and took it

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: הַבַּיִת טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: the house is pure
for I say: he lent it to another and forgot
or that he took it from this corner
and placed it in the other corner and forgot

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the מחלוקת named in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the corner case of חמץ depends on this מחלוקת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the lost axe in a house.

steps.title: Where does the ברייתא mention a corner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא never presents a case of an item found in another corner. So how can our case depend on it?
steps.simpleTranslation: A corner — who mentioned it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the link it just made. The ברייתא's case is a lost axe, not an item found in a different corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case in the ברייתא is an axe that disappeared completely. Our חמץ case is about an item that turned up in a new spot. Corners appear only as one possible excuse in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reasoning. So the ברייתא does not seem to rule on a corner case at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Who mentioned its name? (i.e., this topic was never raised)

phrases.english: A corner — who mentioned it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the use of the ברייתא from step 2 as the source for step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the corner case of חמץ is the מחלוקת in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's case speaks only of a lost axe and never of an item found in a different corner.

steps.title: The ברייתא is missing words: the full version includes a corner case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is incomplete. The full version adds a second case: the axe was put in one corner and found in another. The רבנן say the house is טמא, because an impure person moved it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it is טהור, because the owner moved it and forgot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is missing words, and this is what it teaches: An axe lost in a house, the house is impure, for I say an impure person entered there and took it. Or if he put it in this corner and found it in another corner, the house is impure, for I say an impure person entered there, took it from this corner, and put it in another corner. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: the house is pure, for I say he lent it to another and forgot, or he took it from this corner and put it in that corner and forgot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by filling in words it says are missing from the ברייתא. The added words create a real case of an item that moved corners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the added words, the רבנן explicitly rule on a moved item. They assume someone else moved it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל assumes the owner moved it himself. Now the חמץ case lines up exactly. For the רבנן, the found piece may not be the original, so he should search again. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, it is the same piece, so no new search is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is lacking (words are missing from the text)
And this is what it teaches

steps.whatToRemember: An item that moved to another corner is a real מחלוקת. The רבנן assume an outsider moved it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל assumes the owner moved it and forgot. The חמץ case follows this same מחלוקת.
steps.confusionAlert: חסורי מחסרא does not mean the ברייתא was 'wrong.' It means the גמרא is filling in words that were left out, to show the full scope of what was taught.

phrases.english: It is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
an axe that was lost in a house — the house is impure

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: אָדָם טָמֵא נִכְנַס לְשָׁם וּנְטָלוֹ.
phrases.english: for I say: an impure person entered there and took it
Or if he placed it in this corner
and found it in another corner — the house is impure

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: אָדָם טָמֵא נִכְנַס לְשָׁם
phrases.english: for I say: an impure person entered there

phrases.aramaic: וּנְטָלוֹ מִזָּוִית זוֹ וְהִנִּיחוֹ בְּזָוִית אַחֶרֶת.
phrases.english: and took it from this corner and placed it in another corner

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: הַבַּיִת טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: the house is pure
for I say he lent it to another and forgot
or that he took it from this corner
and placed it in that corner and forgot

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 by filling in the missing text of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא only discusses a lost axe, so it says nothing about an item found in a new corner.
steps.terutzMaskana: The full ברייתא includes a corner case, where the רבנן and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagree. So the חמץ case does depend on their מחלוקת.

steps.title: רבא: a mouse with bread, then crumbs, requires searching
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules about a mouse. If a mouse went in with a loaf in its mouth, and you followed it and found only crumbs, you must search again. Mice do not usually make crumbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A mouse entered with a loaf in its mouth, and he entered after it and found crumbs — it requires searching, because it is not the way of a mouse to make crumbs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new practical rule about בדיקת חמץ. It concerns a mouse that carried bread into an area that was already checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a mouse does not usually make crumbs, the crumbs must come from some other חמץ. That means the whole loaf the mouse brought is still hidden somewhere. So you must search again.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A mouse entered with a loaf in its mouth
and he entered after it and found crumbs
it requires searching

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכּוֹ שֶׁל עַכְבָּר לְפָרֵר.
phrases.english: because it is not the way of a mouse to make crumbs

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: עַכְבָּר נִכְנָס וְכִכָּר בְּפִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate ruling on doubtful חמץ in a house that was already checked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crumbs found after a mouse brought in a loaf do not account for the loaf, so the house must be searched again.

steps.title: רבא: a child with bread, then crumbs, needs no searching
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the opposite ruling about a child. If a child went in with a loaf, and you found crumbs, no new search is needed. Children usually make crumbs, so the crumbs are what is left of that loaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A child entered with a loaf in his hand, and he entered after him and found crumbs — it does not require searching, because it is the way of a child to make crumbs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a matching ruling about a child. This time the result is the opposite of the mouse case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Children usually crumble bread as they eat. So we assume the crumbs are the remains of the loaf the child brought in, and no whole loaf is left hidden. The difference between the two rulings depends only on how each one normally behaves.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's two rulings depend on who carried the bread. A mouse does not make crumbs, so the loaf is still hidden and you must search again. A child does make crumbs, so the crumbs are the loaf and no search is needed.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A child entered with a loaf in his hand
and he entered after him and found crumbs
it does not require searching
because it is the way of a child to make crumbs

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: תִּינוֹק נִכְנָס וְכִכָּר בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The matching opposite of the mouse ruling in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crumbs found after a child brought in a loaf are assumed to be that loaf, so no new search is needed.

steps.title: A mouse with bread enters, and a mouse with bread leaves
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: if a mouse went in with bread and a mouse came out with bread, do we assume it is the same mouse and the same bread?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: A mouse went in with a loaf in its mouth, and a mouse came out with a loaf in its mouth. What is the law? Do we say the one that went in is the same one that came out? Or maybe it is a different one?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question. He asks about a house that was already checked: a mouse brought bread in, and a mouse brought bread out. Do we need a new בדיקה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it is the same mouse with the same bread, then no חמץ is left in the house. If it is a different mouse, the first loaf may still be inside, so we must search again. רבא does not decide. This is the first rung of a ladder of questions.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question (a real doubt he could not settle)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this is about mice for their own sake. The only practical question is whether חמץ is still in a house that was already checked, so that it would need a new בדיקה.

phrases.english: Rava asked:
A mouse enters with a loaf in its mouth,
and a mouse leaves with a loaf in its mouth. What is the law?
Do we say: this is the one that went in,
and this is the one that came out?
Or perhaps it is a different one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the clear rulings on the mouse and the child, רבא raises a case he cannot settle.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When a mouse leaves with bread, may we assume it is the same mouse and the same bread that entered, so that no new בדיקה is needed?

steps.title: A white mouse enters, and a black mouse leaves
steps.stepSummary: Even if we assume it was the same mouse in step 7, what if the mice look different? Did the black mouse take the bread from the white mouse?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the one that went in is the one that came out: a white mouse went in with a loaf, and a black mouse came out with a loaf. What is the law? Is this surely a different loaf? Or maybe the black mouse grabbed it from the white one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא climbs one rung higher. It assumes we treat it as the same mouse in step 7 and asks a harder case, where we can see the mice are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here we know for sure the mouse is different. The only remaining question is whether the bread is the same. One side says a different mouse means different bread. The other side says the black mouse may have snatched the white mouse's bread.

keyTerms.meaning: If you conclude that... (assume the first question is answered this way)
It snatched it away from him

steps.confusionAlert: "If you conclude" does not mean the first question was answered. It only means: suppose it were answered this way. Then here is a harder case.

phrases.aramaic: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר הַיְינוּ הַאי דְּעָל
phrases.english: If you conclude that this is the one that went in
and this is the one that came out:
a white mouse enters with a loaf in its mouth,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַכְבָּר שָׁחוֹר יוֹצֵא וְכִכָּר בְּפִיו, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: and a black mouse leaves with a loaf in its mouth. What is the law?
Is this certainly a different one?
Or perhaps it snatched it from the other one?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר הַיְינוּ הַאי דְּעָל וְהַיְינוּ הַאי דִּנְפַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 7 by assuming one answer to it, then making the case harder.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When the mouse is clearly different, do we still assume it took the same bread from the first mouse?

steps.title: A mouse enters, and a marten leaves with bread
steps.stepSummary: Even if mice don't steal from each other, a חולדה is stronger. Did it take the mouse's bread? Or would it have taken the mouse too?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you conclude that mice do not take from each other: a mouse went in with a loaf, and a חולדה came out with a loaf. What is the law? Did the חולדה surely take it from the mouse? Or maybe it is a different loaf, because if it had taken it from the mouse, the mouse would be found in its mouth too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes one rung higher again. It assumes mice don't steal from each other, since they are about equally strong, and asks about a stronger animal, the חולדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חולדה is strong enough to take the bread, so maybe this is the same loaf. But there is a counter-argument. A חולדה hunts mice, so if it had met this mouse, it would have taken the mouse too. Since only bread is in its mouth, it may be a different loaf.

keyTerms.meaning: A marten or weasel, an animal that hunts mice
They do not take from one another

phrases.english: And if you conclude
that mice do not take from each other:
a mouse enters with a loaf in its mouth,
and a marten leaves with a loaf in its mouth. What is the law?
Did the marten certainly take it from the mouse?
Or perhaps it is a different loaf,
for if it were so that it took it from the mouse,
the mouse would have been found in its mouth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר עַכְבָּרִים לָא שָׁקְלִי מֵהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes one side of step 8, that mice don't steal from each other, and moves to a stronger animal.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a stronger animal leaving with bread mean it took the mouse's bread, or does the missing mouse show it is different bread?

steps.title: The marten leaves holding both the bread and the mouse
steps.stepSummary: Now the חולדה has both the mouse and the bread. Is it surely the same loaf? Or should the bread still be in the mouse's mouth, unless the mouse dropped it in fear?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you conclude that if the חולדה had taken it from the mouse, the mouse would be in its mouth: a mouse went in with a loaf, and a חולדה came out with a loaf and a mouse in its mouth. What is the law? Here it is surely the same one. Or perhaps: if it were the same, the loaf should have been found in the mouse's mouth. Or perhaps the mouse dropped it out of fear, and the חולדה took it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the top rung of the ladder. The objection from step 9 is now answered, because the mouse is in the חולדה's mouth too. The גמרא asks whether that settles it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first this looks certain: same mouse, same bread. But a new objection comes up. The bread should then be in the mouse's mouth, not loose in the חולדה's mouth. The other side of the question is that a frightened mouse may drop its bread, and the חולדה then picked it up separately. None of this is decided, and the next step ends with תיקו.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר אִם אִיתָא דְּמֵעַכְבָּר שְׁקַלְתֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: And if you conclude that if it had taken it from the mouse,
the mouse would be found in its mouth:
a mouse enters with a loaf in its mouth,

phrases.aramaic: וְחוּלְדָּה יוֹצְאָה וְכִכָּר וְעַכְבָּר בְּפִי חוּלְדָּה, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: and a marten leaves with a loaf and a mouse in the marten's mouth. What is the law?
Here it is certainly the same one,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא: אִם אִיתָא דְּאִיהוּ נִיהוּ —
phrases.english: or perhaps: if it were the same one,
the loaf in the mouse's mouth found
should have been found there.
phrases.notes: Phrases 7 and 8 together mean: the loaf should have been found in the mouse's mouth.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא: מִשּׁוּם בִּיעֲתוּתָא הוּא נְפַל, וּשְׁקַלְתֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: Or perhaps: it fell out because of fright, and the marten took it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר אִם אִיתָא דְּמֵעַכְבָּר שְׁקַלְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the reasoning of step 9, that the mouse would be in its mouth, and builds a case where that is fulfilled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When the חולדה holds both the mouse and the bread, may we assume it is the original bread, even though the bread is not in the mouse's mouth?

steps.title: The questions remain unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the whole chain with תיקו: let the questions stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבא's whole ladder of questions without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no proof was found either way. All the questions from steps 7 through 10 stay open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand (the question is left unresolved)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא built a ladder of questions about whether the bread that left the house is the bread that entered it. The ladder goes: same mouse? Different-colored mouse? A חולדה? A חולדה holding both the mouse and the bread? None of these was resolved. It ends in תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chain of questions that began in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's questions about the mouse and the חולדה are left unresolved.

steps.title: A loaf on a high ceiling beam: must he use a ladder?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether a person must climb a ladder to take down a loaf of חמץ sitting on a high ceiling beam.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: If a loaf is on a high beam, does he need a ladder to bring it down, or not? Do we say the רבנן did not make him work this hard, because the loaf won't come down on its own, so he won't come to eat it? Or maybe sometimes it falls, and then he will come to eat it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a new question. He asks if a person must climb a ladder to remove a loaf of חמץ that is up on a high beam.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says this is too much effort. Since the bread will not come down by itself, there is no risk he will eat it. The other side says things on high places sometimes fall, and then he might eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked / raised a question that he could not answer
The top of a high ceiling beam
The Sages did not make him go to this trouble
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new question chain, separate from the mouse questions before it. The topic is no longer 'did the חמץ come back?' It is now 'how much effort must he spend to get rid of חמץ he knows about?'

phrases.english: Rava asked:
a loaf on top of a high beam:
does he need a ladder to take it down,
or does he not need to?
Do we say:
the Rabbis did not make him go to this much trouble,
since it will not come down by itself,
he will not come to eat it.
Or perhaps:
sometimes it falls, and he will come to eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new chain of questions after the mouse chain ended with תיקו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must a person make the effort of climbing a ladder to remove חמץ that will probably never reach him?

steps.title: A loaf in a pit: must he use a ladder to bring it up?
steps.stepSummary: Even if a ladder is needed for the beam, maybe a loaf in a pit is different, since it can never come up on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that sometimes it falls and he comes to eat it: what about a loaf in a pit? Does he need a ladder to bring it up, or not? Here it surely cannot come up by itself. Or perhaps sometimes he goes down to do something he needs, and he will come to eat it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds on step 12. Suppose we decided that a ladder is needed for the beam. Now it asks about a loaf at the bottom of a pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beam case worried that the bread might fall down to him. A pit is different, because bread can never rise up out of a pit on its own. The new worry is the reverse: he might go down into the pit for some reason, find the bread, and eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (assume the first side, then ask a harder case)
His needs (something he has to do)

phrases.english: And if you say
that sometimes it falls and he comes to eat it:
a loaf in a pit:
does he need a ladder to bring it up,
or does he not need to?

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא וַדַּאי דְּלָא עֲבִידָא דְּסָלְקָה מִנַּפְשַׁהּ,
phrases.english: Here it certainly will not come up by itself,
or perhaps:
sometimes he goes down to take care of his needs,
and he will come to eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the stricter answer to step 12 and asks about a case where the bread can never move toward the person.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the chance that he will go down into the pit require him to remove bread that cannot come up on its own?

steps.title: A loaf in a snake's mouth: must he pay a snake charmer?
steps.stepSummary: Even if a ladder is needed for the pit, must he hire a snake charmer, which costs money, to get bread out of a snake's mouth?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that sometimes he goes down for his needs and comes to eat it: what about a loaf in a snake's mouth? Does he need a snake charmer to take it out, or not? Do the רבנן make him put in his own body's effort, but not spend his money? Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third question in the chain. It asks whether a person must hire a snake charmer to get חמץ out of a snake's mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is money. Climbing a ladder costs only effort, but a snake charmer must be paid. Maybe the רבנן demand effort from his body but not from his wallet. Or maybe both are the same, and he must remove the חמץ any way he can.
steps.whyThisMatters: This question brings in a new idea: the obligation of physical effort (גוף) may be separate from the obligation to spend money (ממון).

phrases.english: If you say
that sometimes he goes down for his needs and comes to eat it:
a loaf in the mouth of a snake:
does he need a snake charmer to take it out,
or does he not need to?
With his body, the Rabbis made him go to trouble,
but with his money, the Rabbis did not make him go to trouble.
Or perhaps there is no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the stricter answer to step 13 and moves from physical effort to spending money.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the duty to remove חמץ include spending money, or only personal effort?

steps.title: The questions remain unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רבא's chain with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives no answer to this chain of questions and closes it with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether the רבנן require a ladder or a snake charmer. All three questions (beam, pit, snake) stay open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רבא asked three questions, each harder than the last: a ladder for a beam, a ladder for a pit, and paying a snake charmer. The last one asks whether spending money (ממון) is different from personal effort (גוף). All three end in תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chain of questions from steps 12 through 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The questions about a ladder and a snake charmer are left unresolved.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's three search times
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens with רבי יהודה, who lists three times for searching for חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: We search on the night of the 14th, on the morning of the 14th, and at the time we destroy the חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי יהודה names three times connected to the search for חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three times are the night of the 14th of ניסן, the next morning, and the hour of ביעור (destroying the חמץ). The משנה does not yet say whether all three searches are required or whether these are just the allowed times. That exact question will come up in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the core text being studied)
The night that begins the 14th of ניסן
The time when the חמץ is destroyed

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful: the משנה does not clearly say whether רבי יהודה requires three separate searches. The גמרא below discusses exactly this.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One searches on the evening of the fourteenth,
and on the fourteenth in the morning,
and at the time of the removal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בּוֹדְקִין אוֹר אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after רבא's chain ended in תיקו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: one searches on the night of the 14th, on the morning of the 14th, and at the time of ביעור.

steps.title: The חכמים: if you missed it, search later
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that someone who missed the search keeps making it up: on the 14th, during the מועד, and even after the מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: If he did not search on the night of the 14th, he should search on the day of the 14th. If he did not search on the 14th, he should search during the holiday. If he did not search during the holiday, he should search after the holiday.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה. They give a chain of 'make-up' times for someone who missed the search.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the main search is on the night of the 14th, and the later times are only backups if he missed it. They let him search even after פסח, because חמץ that a Jew owned during פסח (חמץ שעבר עליו הפסח) is forbidden and must be destroyed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole מחלוקת. Does רבי יהודה require three searches, or does he only limit the latest time a person may search? The גמרא will debate this.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
If one did not search on the evening of the fourteenth,
he should search on the fourteenth.
If he did not search on the fourteenth,
he should search during the festival.
If he did not search during the festival,
he should search after the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: לֹא בָּדַק אוֹר אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: whoever missed the search makes it up on the 14th, during the מועד, or even after the מועד.

steps.title: Put away leftover חמץ carefully
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds a practical rule: חמץ kept after the search must be stored in a hidden, safe place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whatever חמץ he leaves over, he should put in a hidden place, so that he will not need to search again after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a practical tip. The חמץ you keep after the search (for example, to eat in the morning) should be put away safely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the leftover חמץ is left out in the open, a child or animal might carry it off. Then the house would need another search. Putting it in a careful, hidden spot prevents that problem.

phrases.english: And what he leaves over, he should place in a concealed spot,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא צָרִיךְ בְּדִיקָה אַחֲרָיו.
phrases.english: so that he will not need to search after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a general practical rule at the end of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover חמץ must be stored carefully so that no new search becomes necessary.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה teaches three things: רבי יהודה's three times, the חכמים's make-up searches (even after פסח), and that leftover חמץ must be stored safely.

steps.title: Why three times for רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the reason behind רבי יהודה's three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why רבי יהודה listed exactly three times. This question sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes that רבי יהודה requires three searches, and it asks where that number comes from. Later, רב יוסף will question this very assumption.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's first opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or logic for רבי יהודה's three times.

steps.title: Three פסוקים about removing חמץ
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא explain that the three searches match three פסוקים in the תורה about removing חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא both say: It matches the three times the תורה mentions removing חמץ: 'No חמץ shall be seen with you, and no leaven shall be seen with you'; 'Seven days no leaven shall be found in your houses'; 'But on the first day you shall remove leaven from your houses.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer together. Each search matches one פסוק that talks about getting rid of חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה uses three different phrases: 'not seen' (לא יראה), 'not found' (לא ימצא), and 'remove' (תשביתו). This answer reads them as three removals, so רבי יהודה requires three actual searches.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna
who both say:
Corresponding to the three removals in the Torah:
"No leavened bread shall be seen with you,
neither shall leaven be seen with you" (Exodus 13:7);
"Seven days no leaven shall be found in your houses" (Exodus 12:19);
"Yet on the first day you shall remove leaven from your houses" (Exodus 12:15).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three searches correspond to three פסוקים that speak about removing חמץ.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the three times are only a window
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף cites a ברייתא and argues that רבי יהודה does not require three searches. The three times are just the deadline window, and the real argument is about searching after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: רבי יהודה says, 'Anyone who did not search at these three times may not search anymore.' This shows that they argue about what happens from this point on.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges the answer of step 20 using a ברייתא. In that ברייתא, רבי יהודה says that once the three times have passed, a person can no longer search.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the three times sound like three chances to search, not three required searches. So the מחלוקת is not about how many searches are needed. It is about whether one may still search after the time of ביעור: the חכמים say yes, and רבי יהודה says no. This undermines the idea that the three searches match three פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection (usually from an earlier source)

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not saying that רבי יהודה denies the obligation to search. He is saying that the three times are opportunities to search, not three separate requirements.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection:
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁלֹּא בָּדַק בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה פְּרָקִים הַלָּלוּ —
phrases.english: Anyone who did not search at these three times
may no longer search.
Apparently, it is from this point onward that they disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה requires three searches corresponding to three פסוקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא presents the three times as the window for searching, after which one may no longer search. So the מחלוקת is about searching after the window, not about the number of searches.

steps.title: מר זוטרא's version of רב יוסף's objection
steps.stepSummary: In מר זוטרא's version of רב יוסף's objection, the ברייתא says 'at one of these three times'. This proves that רבי יהודה does not require three searches and that the argument is only about searching afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא taught it this way: רב יוסף objected. רבי יהודה says: anyone who did not search at one of these three times may no longer search. So the argument must be about whether he may search afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב יוסף's challenge. In this version the wording of the ברייתא is even stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'at one of these three times' show that one search at any of the three times is enough. That means the three times are only a window of opportunity, not three required searches. This directly attacks the explanation of רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא that the three times match three פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught it this way (introduces a different version of the same discussion)
Raised an objection from a source
Times / set periods (here, the three chances to search)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new challenge. It is the same objection of רב יוסף from step 21, recorded in מר זוטרא's version with slightly different wording.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra taught it this way:
Rav Yosef raised an objection:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Anyone who did not search
at one of these three times
phrases.notes: 'One of' means a single search is enough.

phrases.english: may no longer search.
Apparently, it is about 'he may no longer search'
that they disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא מַתְנֵי הָכִי: מֵתִיב רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Alternate version of the same objection from step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation in step 20 that רבי יהודה requires three searches based on three פסוקים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says 'one of these three times', so one search is enough. The three times are just a deadline window.

steps.title: רבי יהודה also means 'if he did not search'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the objection. רבי יהודה, like the חכמים, is only describing what to do if someone missed the search.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יהודה also is saying: 'if he did not search' at the first time, he searches at the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the 'three פסוקים' explanation. It agrees that רבי יהודה is talking about making up a missed search.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, we thought רבי יהודה required three searches. Now both sides agree that one search is the basic requirement and the later times are make-up chances. This sets up the next question: what exactly are they arguing about?
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's three times are not three required searches. They are three chances to make up a missed search.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yehuda too
is saying 'if he did not search'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נָמֵי, אִם לֹא בָּדַק קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רב יוסף's objection and retracts the explanation of step 20
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both רבי יהודה and the חכמים speak about making up a missed search; neither requires three searches.

steps.title: The real argument: a decree after the prohibition begins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה allows the search only before eating חמץ becomes forbidden, because of a גזירה that the person might eat some. The רבנן do not make that גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is what they argue about. רבי יהודה holds: before the prohibition, yes, he searches; after the prohibition, no. This is a גזירה, in case he comes to eat some of the חמץ. The רבנן hold: we do not make that גזירה.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that both sides agree the search can be made up, the גמרא explains the true point of their argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is about searching after חמץ becomes forbidden to eat. רבי יהודה worries that someone holding a piece of bread he finds might forget and eat it, so he stops the search at that point. The רבנן are not worried, so the search continues even during and after the מועד.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition (here, the time when eating חמץ becomes forbidden)
A rabbinic decree made to prevent a mistake
We do not make a decree

steps.whyThisMatters: This defines the whole argument in the משנה. It also sets up the next challenge: does רבי יהודה really worry that people will eat forbidden food they are handling?

phrases.english: And here, this is what they disagree about:
One master (Rabbi Yehuda) holds:
before the prohibition, yes (he searches);
after the prohibition, no,
a decree, lest
he come to eat from it.
And the Rabbis hold: we do not make that decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having dropped the earlier explanation, the גמרא gives a new explanation of the argument
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: no search once eating חמץ is forbidden, because of a גזירה that he might eat it. רבנן: no such גזירה, so the search continues.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really fear people will eat? The עומר markets
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבי יהודה makes this גזירה. A משנה shows that the markets of ירושלים were full of new grain right after the עומר. That grain must have been prepared while it was still forbidden, with no worry that people would eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really make a גזירה in case someone eats from it? But we learned in a משנה: once the עומר was offered, people would go out and find the markets of ירושלים full of flour and roasted grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason just given for רבי יהודה. It does this by pointing to a case where people handled forbidden food and no one worried they would eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New grain (חדש) is forbidden until the עומר is offered. If the markets were already full of flour and roasted grain right after the עומר, people must have harvested and processed it while it was still forbidden. The גמרא will go on to connect this practice to רבי יהודה, so the question is why he isn't worried here that they would eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה
The barley offering on the 16th of ניסן that permits new grain

steps.confusionAlert: The flour and roasted grain are from the new crop. They could only be ready right after the עומר if the work was done while the grain was still forbidden to eat. That is the whole point of the challenge.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda decree
in case he comes to eat from it?
But didn't we learn:
once the omer was offered
they would go out and find
the markets of Jerusalem
full of flour and roasted grain.
phrases.notes: This grain was prepared while new grain was still forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי גָּזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה דִּילְמָא אָתֵי לְמֵיכַל מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason just given for רבי יהודה's view
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 24 that רבי יהודה makes a גזירה in case one eats forbidden food he is handling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: People processed new grain while it was forbidden, and no one worried they would eat it. So why worry about someone searching for חמץ?
